title: How can a rectangle be cut into a rhombus of the same area?
description: A rectangle is cut across its middle, and each half is cut along a diagonal to give four matching right triangles. Their right angles are put together at one centre, which makes a rhombus whose diagonals are the length and twice the width.
teaching_notes: One idea: four matching right triangles with their right angles together make a rhombus with the same area as the rectangle. Watch for students who join the triangles along the wrong sides.

source: Figure it Out (rhombus and trapezium, question 2)
video_script.why: The child uses the four right triangles of a rhombus from the solved example, in reverse, to turn a rectangle into a rhombus.
video_script.substitution: Cut the rectangle into four right triangles and put their right angles together.

video_script.payoff_line: Cut into four right triangles and put the right angles together at the centre

final_answer.value: cut into four right triangles and put the right angles together at the centre
final_answer.spoken: cut into four right triangles and put the right angles together at the centre

maths_rules: rectangle with length L and width W; cut across the middle into two halves, each L/2 by W
cut each half along a diagonal: four matching right triangles with legs L/2 and W

placed with their right angles together at one centre, the triangles make a rhombus with diagonals L and 2W, since the legs L/2 along one line on both sides give L and the legs W along the other line give 2W
area = 1/2 × L × 2W = L × W, the rectangle's area; check with L = 8, W = 3: legs 4 and 3, sides 5, diagonals 8 and 6, 1/2 × 8 × 6 = 24 = 8 × 3
video_script.design: One rectangle all video: cut across the middle, cut each half on its diagonal, and put the four right angles together.
